name: Octopus.do
tagline: Free visual sitemap builder with lo-fi wireframes for planning website structure
description: Octopus.do is a visual sitemap builder for planning website architecture. You map pages, add lo-fi wireframe blocks and content, and share the plan with others. It can generate a sitemap with AI or crawl an existing site, and it has a ChatGPT app. The core builder is free, with paid plans.
agent_guidance: Use it to agree on page structure before visual design starts. Export the map into the brief for designers and agents.
why_it_matters: It makes information architecture visible early in a web project.
tier_reason: A practical, free planning tool for site structure.

name: omou
tagline: Minimal Gmail client built around keyboard shortcuts, search, and a calm interface
description: omou is a minimal Gmail client for people who prefer keyboard shortcuts, command palettes, and search. It keeps the Gmail data model but removes most of the noise around it. A demo is available, and the full app is behind an email sign-up.
agent_guidance: Use it as a reference for a calm, keyboard-first mail interface. Try the demo before you join the list.
why_it_matters: It is a clean example of reducing a familiar interface to essentials.
tier_reason: A mail app, useful only as an interface reference.

name: Keeper.sh
tagline: Open-source calendar sync that marks you busy across Google, Outlook, iCloud, and Fastmail
description: Keeper.sh copies events between personal, work, and school calendars so all of them show you as busy at the same times. It supports Google Calendar, Outlook, iCloud, Fastmail, and CalDAV, and event titles stay private. It is open source under the AGPL-3.0 license, with a hosted plan.
agent_guidance: Use it to stop double-booking across several calendars. Self-host it if you do not want a third party to see your calendars.
why_it_matters: It solves a common scheduling problem with a privacy-first approach.
evidence: https://www.keeper.sh/ (HTTP 200, page fetched 2026-10-09), https://github.com/ridafkih/keeper.sh (GitHub API, 1381 stars), depo.zip listing https://www.depo.zip/tools/j576spknp9byg66aqvrr54w92n84pthc
tier_reason: A calendar utility outside interface design work.

name: OpenSec
tagline: Donated AI security reviews for public GitHub repositories, run on donors' spare AI usage
description: OpenSec lets maintainers request a private AI security review of a public GitHub repository. Donors run the report with their own Claude or Codex capacity. The reviews run on Vercel's deepsec tool.
agent_guidance: Use it to get a free security review for an open-source library. Treat the findings as leads to verify, not as final results.
why_it_matters: It pools spare AI capacity for open-source security.

name: Pallyy
tagline: Social media scheduler for creators and agencies, with client approval links and an API
description: Pallyy plans, schedules, and publishes social content across platforms for creators and agencies. Clients approve posts through a shared link, and pricing is per client, not per channel. A new API is available.
agent_guidance: Use it to plan launch posts and get client sign-off in one place. Preview each post on every platform before it goes out.
why_it_matters: It simplifies approval for agency social work.
tier_reason: A marketing tool outside interface design work.

name: Play with Putty
tagline: Google Labs experiment in simple, collaborative vibe coding, open by waitlist
description: Play with Putty is an experiment from Google Labs in collaborative vibe coding. Several people build software together with AI in a simple shared space. Access is through a waitlist.
agent_guidance: Join the waitlist if you want early access. There is no public product to evaluate yet.
why_it_matters: It shows Google exploring multiplayer AI building.
tier_reason: Announced only, with no public product.

name: Port Menu

description: Port Menu is a macOS menu bar app that tracks dev servers across projects. It shows each server's project, port, and uptime, with buttons to open or kill it. The source is on GitHub.

why_it_matters: It keeps local development tidy.

name: Ports
tagline: Free native macOS menu bar app that shows every localhost dev server with CPU and memory
description: Ports is a free, native macOS menu bar app that lists every dev server on localhost. It shows the port, project, uptime, CPU, and memory, with one-click terminal and kill actions. It needs macOS 14 or later and publishes checksums for its downloads.
agent_guidance: Use it to find which project holds a port. Verify the download checksum before you install it.
why_it_matters: It makes background dev servers visible.
tier_reason: A developer utility outside interface design work.

name: Productboard
tagline: Agentic product management system for understanding customers and prioritizing features
description: Productboard is a product management system that helps teams understand customer needs, prioritize features, and align on a roadmap. Productboard Spark adds an AI agent with context across the product and customers. It has more than 25 integrations and a free trial.
agent_guidance: Use it to connect customer feedback to roadmap decisions. Agree on a feedback tagging scheme before you import data.
why_it_matters: It is a standard tool for product discovery work.
tier_reason: A product management app outside interface design work.

name: Quo
tagline: Shared phone system for small businesses with calls, texts, and an AI agent, formerly OpenPhone
description: Quo, formerly OpenPhone, is a shared phone system for startups and small businesses. Calls, texts, and contacts live in one AI-powered workspace with shared numbers, routing, and analytics. It has an API, an MCP server, and the Sona AI agent.
agent_guidance: Use it to share a support phone line across a small team. It has no role in interface design work.
why_it_matters: It is a modern business phone system.
tier_reason: A phone service outside interface design work.

name: React Doctor
tagline: Static analysis that finds risky, repeated, and inaccessible React code for agents to fix
description: React Doctor finds problems in React code with deterministic static analysis. It flags complex functions, repeated JSX, and correctness, performance, security, accessibility, and maintainability risks. Coding agents use its report to fix the code. The team also publishes React Bench, which compares how models handle React.
agent_guidance: Use it after an agent writes React components, so repeated JSX and accessibility gaps get caught early. Feed the report back to the agent as a task list.
why_it_matters: It gives agent-written UI code a deterministic quality check.

name: Readout
tagline: macOS dashboard that shows your dev environment at a glance instead of terminal tabs
description: Readout, by Benji Taylor, is a macOS app that shows your development environment in one dashboard instead of six terminal tabs. It is in beta at version 0.0.11 and needs macOS Tahoe.
agent_guidance: Use it if terminal tabs hide the state of your local services. It is an early beta.
why_it_matters: It is a calm, designed view of developer state.
tier_reason: An early beta utility outside interface design work.

name: Squark
